title: rerere silently resolves the reconciler's merges using a human's recorded resolutions
description:
git rerere is enabled GLOBALLY on this host (~/.gitconfig [rerere] enabled = true). The reconciler merges attempt branches in the operator's checkout, so it shares .git/rr-cache — which currently holds 28 recorded resolutions, every one of them recorded by a PERSON resolving a conflict by hand.

Observed live 2026-09-19: 9fc attempt 6 was refused with

    merge_failed: attempt 6 of 9fc does not merge onto epic/ncv:
    Recorded preimage for 'cloudflare/src/epic-reconciler.ts'

That line is rerere's, not the conflict's. So rerere is active inside the reconciler's merge, and it is doing two things nobody asked it to:

1. RECORDING preimages from the run's merges, polluting a human's resolution cache with machine conflicts.
2. REPLAYING a human's earlier hand resolution into a machine merge. THIS IS THE DANGEROUS HALF. A resolution recorded while a person merged branch A onto B is re-applied, silently and without review, to a DIFFERENT merge that happens to present the same conflict text. The run then gates and integrates a tree nobody looked at, and the evidence says the merge was clean.

This matters more here than in an ordinary repo because the whole design rests on durable evidence being a true statement about a tree. A silently re-resolved conflict makes the tree something no party chose: not the worker's, not the base's, and not a reviewer's.

Work:
- The reconciler must set -c rerere.enabled=false (or GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY/VALUE) on every merge it performs, so the host's config cannot reach into it. Same category as GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0: the run states its own environment rather than inheriting one.
- Consider the same for rerere.autoupdate.
- The refusal must carry the CONFLICT, not rerere's chatter — see 44q, which this makes more urgent: the operator was handed 'Recorded preimage for ...' as the entire reason a merge failed.
- Test: a merge whose conflict text matches a poisoned rr-cache entry must still conflict and refuse, not resolve itself.

Found while resuming Phase 4. The host's 28 cached resolutions include several I recorded by hand today while resolving the biome and rescue merges.
